title: The Passion Crucible Practice
opening: You like the idea of publishing but have not experienced revising a piece after specific critique. Test one real demand of a possible passion at a safe, bounded scale; the test is the work itself.

labels.figure: A plan names the value, question, and limits; the actual attempt produces observations that inform whether to continue, adjust, or reconsider.

labels.valueObserved: Did the value remain compelling during the work? What did I notice?

source.manuscript: The Passion Crucible Practice: choose a bounded difficulty directly relevant to a possible passion; state the value and what the attempt should reveal, with limits; make the attempt and observe both difficulty and whether the value remains compelling; then review whether you would choose that work again and decide to continue, adjust or reconsider.
source.attribution: Supplied recovered manuscript; authorship/adoption of every wording is not independently established.
source.boundary: A challenge must be relevant to the pursuit. Unrelated pain, humiliation or unsafe exposure does not establish passion. One unrepresentative trial cannot stand for an entire pursuit. A difficulty can be informative without being proof; stop or change the trial if safety or access conditions require it.

example.title: The task is learning to teach
example.body: Illustrative case: someone is considering teaching. They prepare one short explanation of a topic they know, share it with a willing learner, and ask which step was unclear. They plan to revise that explanation once, then stop. Their value is helping another person understand; the question is whether explanation and revision still feel worthwhile when a learner misunderstands. The plan is not the evidence. Afterward they record what they actually did, how revision felt, and whether they would choose another teaching task. A learner's confusion is a relevant demand; hostile treatment is not a teaching test. If the small lesson does not resemble the teaching work they mean to pursue, they keep the conclusion narrow.

comparison.title: A smaller trial can answer the question
comparison.body: Near miss: deliberately making the work harder, accepting humiliation, or enduring unrelated pain to prove commitment. None tests whether the pursuit's value remains compelling. A single short explanation and one revision can be enough to learn something.

connections: Connect this with Value > Suffering (M070) to examine value during difficulty, Minimum Viable Action Design (M117) to bound a test, and Difficulty Diagnostic (M076) to distinguish sources of resistance.
